candidates: Proofread variable and identifier names in test files for typos before committing (e.g., `flwoDiagram1` instead of `flowDiagram1`).

Test names should be professional and descriptive; avoid informal or humorous wording. When a test targets a specific diagram type, include the diagram name in the test name or in a surrounding `describe` block (e.g., `describe('flowchart', () => { it('should not modify db when rendering different diagrams', ...) })`).

When testing that `getDiagramFromText()` produces independent DB instances for different diagram renderings, do not rely solely on object identity (`expect(db1).not.toBe(db2)`). Also assert that concrete DB state values differ between the two instances (e.g., render diagrams with different directions and call `getDirection()` on each DB to compare), and use `instanceof` to confirm the correct DB class type.

When writing isolation/independence tests for a diagram type that still uses a singleton or shared DB, mark the test with `it.fails` (or `test.fails`) and include an inline comment explaining the known limitation (e.g., `// SequenceDiagram currently uses a singleton DB, so this test will fail`).

Do not commit personal developer scratch or playground files (e.g., `cypress/platform/<username>.html`) to the repository. These files are local dev artifacts that add noise to the project's git history.

When implementing a DB class for a JISON-based diagram parser, all methods invoked from the JISON grammar file must be accessible as own (direct) properties on the DB object—not just on its prototype—because JISON copies only own properties when building the parser. The conventional pattern in this codebase is to bind prototype methods in the constructor (e.g., `this.addVertex = this.addVertex.bind(this);`). Add a comment in the class explaining this JISON constraint so future maintainers do not accidentally remove the bindings. Also verify that any new syntax used (e.g., public class instance fields) does not break support for the project's minimum-supported browser targets.

Keep structural refactors (e.g., converting a module to class-based architecture) strictly non-behavioral: do not bundle default-parameter changes, logic changes, or any observable behavior differences in the same PR. Open a separate PR for each behavioral change so the refactor's diff remains reviewable in isolation.
Diagram DB classes must explicitly declare `implements DiagramDB` in their class definition and follow the project naming convention of an all-uppercase `DB` suffix (e.g., `FlowDB`, not `FlowDb`).

When pushing a class method into a callback or function array (e.g., `this.funs.push(...)`), always attach `.bind(this)` to preserve the correct `this` context at call time (e.g., `this.funs.push(this.setupToolTips.bind(this))`).

In diagram DB classes, call `getConfig()` only inside `clear()` (the designated state-reset method), not inside per-operation methods such as `addVertex`, and not redundantly in the constructor if the constructor already calls `clear()`. Similarly, avoid calling state-setter methods (e.g., `setGen()`) in the constructor when `clear()` already initializes that same state, to prevent double-initialization.

When a diagram DB class is refactored to instance-based architecture but certain lifecycle methods (e.g., title/accessibility getters and setters) still delegate to the shared `commonDb`, document this explicitly in both the PR description and a code comment. Include a link to the discussion or issue explaining why those functions were not moved to per-instance state (e.g., parser integration constraints or `DiagramDB` interface requirements).

When declaring private or protected class fields that may be absent, explicitly annotate their type as `T | undefined` (e.g., `private direction: string | undefined`). Initialize numeric counter fields with their default value inline (e.g., `private secCount = -1`) rather than leaving them uninitialized and relying on implicit `undefined`.

Changeset entries should describe the observable behavioral change from a user's perspective—what API or behavior changed and what it now does—rather than summarizing the internal implementation change (e.g., prefer `` fix: `mermaidAPI.getDiagramFromText()` now returns a new db for each flowchart `` over `refactor: convert FlowDB to class-based architecture`).
